title: Codex Ratchet candidate fuel package
description: Structural shape of one candidate package P = (claim, assumptions, carrier, nesting_order, implementation, predictions, rivals, known_failure_modes) plus a provenance sub-schema, per owner spec. This schema describes what a candidate SHOULD carry to be adequate fuel for the pairwise ratchet. It does not itself rank, admit, or compare candidates -- computing relative MSS / presumption / any tooth is the ratchet's job (code run on executable finite structures), never this schema and never an LLM narrative. See fuel_gate/README.md and system_v8/candidates/RANKING_VOID_llm_did_ratchets_job.md for the incident that makes this boundary explicit.

claim.description: The one-sentence conditional proposal this candidate makes. Stays conditional ('if a finite ratchet needs X, then...'), never asserted as settled fact.

assumptions.description: Named commitments the carrier installs (e.g. positivity, unit trace, associativity). Every commitment a rival could point to should be named here or in known_failure_modes, not left implicit.

carrier.description: Short machine-comparable identifier for the underlying mathematical carrier family (e.g. 'finite_density_matrix_clifford_spinor_ideal'). The fuel-adequacy gate reads this verbatim to detect candidates that are relabeled copies of one another (same carrier + same model family + same order).

nesting_order.description: Short machine-comparable identifier for the schedule direction (e.g. 'bottom_up_0to8', 'top_down_12to0'). Used by the fuel-adequacy gate's effective-candidate collapse rule.

kind.description: 'prose_spec' = markdown only, no code. 'partial' = some layers reuse or wire to already-executed code. 'executable_code' = the candidate itself runs.

implementation.description: What actually exists on disk for this candidate today. Honesty-forcing: a candidate cannot claim executable-enough status merely by describing probes in prose if implementation.kind says prose_spec.

predictions.description: Concrete, checkable predictions this candidate makes -- what a probe should show if the candidate is right.

rivals.description: Named rival carriers or candidates this one should be run against.

known_failure_modes.description: Ways this candidate is already known or suspected to be beatable. An empty list here is itself a red flag, not a clean bill of health.

model.description: Model family that generated this candidate, as a short slug (e.g. 'openai_gpt_codex', 'xai_grok', 'anthropic_claude'). This is the field the fuel-adequacy gate buckets on for 'distinct model families' -- keep it a stable short slug, not a long free-text description, or diversity counting breaks.

version.description: Version, build, or session label within the model family (e.g. 'sonnet', 'haiku', 'terra'). Free text; not used for family bucketing.

prompt_lineage.description: The prompt or prompt chain that produced this candidate. If genuinely untracked, say so explicitly ('unknown -- no session log captured') rather than omitting the key -- an explicit unknown is a thin-provenance flag the gate can detect; a missing key is a harder failure.

source_corpus.description: What source material (docs, prior receipts, repo files) the candidate draws on, if known. Nullable -- 'if known' per owner spec -- but the key must be present.

tools.description: Tools or skills used to produce the candidate.

saw_preferred_answer.description: Did the generating process see the owner's preferred/reference answer before producing this candidate? Must be a real boolean. Writing the string 'unknown' is a type violation, on purpose: not knowing whether a candidate saw the answer key is a real, reportable defect, not a detail to shrug off.

inherited_assumptions.description: Assumptions inherited from cited prior work, distinct from the candidate's own new assumptions in the top-level 'assumptions' field.

code_lineage.description: What code, if any, this candidate reuses or extends (e.g. a specific script and function name). Nullable when no code exists -- but say so explicitly rather than omitting the key.

counterarguments.description: Known objections to this candidate, including from rival candidates or audits. Optional -- not required for provenance-adequacy, but strongly encouraged.

rejected_alternatives.description: Alternatives considered and rejected in favor of this candidate's carrier/order, with the reason. Optional -- not required for provenance-adequacy, but strongly encouraged.

variation_slot.description: The six required fuel-pool roles the fuel-adequacy gate checks for coverage. Not a package field -- which slot a candidate fills is a pool-relative role assigned in the provenance manifest's wrapper entry, not an intrinsic property of the candidate itself.
